title: Mitral annular disjunction associated with myxomatous mitral valve disease, infundibular pulmonic stenosis and ventricular septal defect in a dog: a case report.
journal: Journal of veterinary cardiology : the official journal of the European Society of Veterinary Cardiology
abstract: Mitral annular disjunction is an abnormality of the mitral valve characterized by a displacement of the mitral annulus in which the annulus is functionally decoupled from the left ventricle and moves toward the atrium during systole. In human medicine, it is commonly associated with an increased risk of mitral valve prolapse, cardiac arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death but rarely described in veterinary medicine. This article describes a case report of a six-year-old male Shih tzu dog with signs of frequent syncope episodes diagnosed by echocardiography with mitral annular disjunction associated with myxomatous mitral valve disease, infundibular pulmonic stenosis, and perimembranous ventricular septal defect with bidirectional shunting. Due to the patient's congenital heart defects, clinical signs, and laboratory results, the hemodynamic profile was determined to be functionally analogous to the Tetralogy of Fallot. Conservative drug therapy with β-blocker propranolol was chosen rather than a surgical approach. Short-term follow-up showed initial improvement of clinical signs, followed by progressive worsening. The total survival time was 19 months from the initial diagnosis and the conservative palliative therapy. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first report of mitral annular disjunction associated with congenital abnormalities in dogs.
